narrative.overview:
Brainless feels like a practical control surface used during live store operations: immediately scannable, touch-ready, and explicit about state. Its visual identity has two established expressions. Club uses warm paper, dark ink, coral signals, solid surfaces, and restrained lift; Classic uses a near-black violet canvas, translucent panels, indigo-to-violet emphasis, and brighter depth effects.

New operational surfaces inherit the selected theme instead of blending them. Information is organized into readable cards, compact filters, status badges, and focused work areas; the interface makes shared state and the next action visible.
keyCharacteristics: Two complete themes with shared hierarchy and interaction behavior.
Dense but readable operational layouts with clear selected states.
Rounded rectangular controls, pill filters, and at least 44px touch targets.
Coral is Club's action signal; indigo and violet carry the same role in Classic.
Traditional Chinese copy and the cat mark remain part of the product identity.

rules.name: The Theme Integrity Rule
rules.body: Use one theme's palette as a complete set; never place Club coral-and-paper components inside Classic violet glass, or vice versa.

rules.name: The Signal Rarity Rule
rules.body: Reserve coral, indigo, and semantic colors for actions, selection, focus, and status—not broad decorative fields.

rules.name: The Scan-Then-Read Rule
rules.body: Let weight and spacing identify title, state, and metadata before the user reads the longer body copy.

rules.name: The First-Action Rule
rules.body: Put the page promise and primary create action before dense operational content; put search, filters, and sorting directly above the queue they control.

rules.name: The Structural Depth Rule
rules.body: Elevation communicates stickiness, selection, overlays, or focused work; ordinary content surfaces remain quiet.

dos: Do preserve identical information hierarchy and touch behavior across Club and Classic.
Do keep shared state—status, vote count, author/store, timestamps, and errors—visible at the point of action.
Do use the 8px / 12px / 16px corner hierarchy consistently.
Do disable nonessential motion under reduced-motion preferences.
donts: Don't mix theme primitives within a component or surface.
Don't hide operational status inside body copy or a secondary dialog.
Don't turn dense work queues into chat walls; preserve list scanability and a focused thread.
Don't make a user create a duplicate when search and similar-item review can route them to an existing discussion.
